newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Only one Indonesia state company to float in '97.
newsitem.headline: Only one Indonesia state company to float in '97.

text.p: Indonesian mining company Aneka Tambang will be the only state-owned enterprise to be floated this year, a senior finance ministry official said on Thursday.

Director-General of State Enterprises Bacelius Ruru said issues pertaining to regulatory framework were hindering the privatisation of other state-owned companies, particularly those that enjoy monopolies.
Ruru said the government views privatisation as an important tool for improving the performance of public enterprises.

"There are many others that are being prepared, such as (state electricity utility) PLN, Krakatau Steel and (toll road operator) Jasa Marga, but at this moment it is only Aneka Tambang, scheduled for the fourth quarter," Ruru told reporters at the sidelines of a capital markets conference.
"Bringing a state-owned enterprise into the capital market has so many things to do with the regulatory framework," he said. "There are a lot of state-owned enterprises with natural monopolies."
Ruru said PLN and Jasa Marga involved monopolies, and the regulatory framework for these sectors would have to be settled before they could be privatised.
He said the government had restructured the regulatory framework of the telecommunications sector before it privatised PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Telkom) and Indonesia Satellite Corp (Indosat).

"At the same time, as we are preparing them for IPOs we are doing this restructuring and streamlining of the regulatory framework, and this is the reason why this year it is only Aneka Tambang (that is being listed)," Ruru said.
